primitives.note: Darkness Rise basic attack bonus magic damage (40% AP), proc damage
3 stacks (from autos/Q/E hits) within 4s each grant Darkness Rise: MS + damaging aura
Darkness Rise aura: persistent area damage per second while active, scales with target max HP and AP
Obliterate and Death's Grasp deal on-cast (or fixed-delay) damage on cooldown
Obliterate deals increased damage (1.3x-1.5x) if it hits only one (isolated) enemy
Indestructible passive converts damage dealt/taken into Potential Shield resource
Indestructible: cast to shield, recast to convert remaining shield into heal
Realm of Death reduces target's current AP, total AS, max HP, armor, MR, size, base AD by 10% for duration
true damage from 10% max-HP reduction, ignores resistances/shields, floors target at 1 HP
Mordekaiser heals for 10% of target's max HP and gains stolen stats (survival-fight relevant, not self-damage but stat/HP transfer)
Potential Shield / shield-to-heal conversion primarily matters for the survival fight, not damage output

needsBespoke.why: Mordekaiser's W (Indestructible) is a resource-conversion shield/heal system (Potential Shield banked from % of damage dealt and taken, capped at 30% max HP with decay and a recast-to-heal mechanic) that the closed primitive list only approximates via stat-conversion + recast-or-multipart; a faithful survival-fight simulation needs bespoke logic tracking the Potential Shield meter (gain rates, decay, min/max caps, recast conversion to healing) rather than a generic timed shield. Additionally R's stat-steal (multi-stat theft applied to both caster and target simultaneously, including base AD reduction computed off current total AD, plus 'keeps stats if target dies') is a bespoke dual-buff/debuff transfer not cleanly covered by target-debuff alone.

proposal: Pre-fight: assume Darkness Rise passive stacks are at zero (no prior combat) and Potential Shield (W) meter is empty at the start.

Open with Realm of Death (R) on the dummy if available, to secure the 10% max-HP true damage, the heal, and the stat-steal buff before committing to the rest of the burst (only usable once given ~140-100s cooldown, so it lands at most once in the 15s window).
Immediately follow with Death's Grasp (E) for its magic damage and to build a Darkness Rise stack.
Follow with Obliterate (Q) for its high-scaling magic damage (isolated bonus applies since dummy is the only enemy) and another Darkness Rise stack.

Weave in basic attacks throughout (each auto contributes on-hit Darkness Rise bonus damage and builds a stack toward the 3-stack Darkness Rise aura); once 3 stacks are reached, Darkness Rise's damaging aura ticks automatically each second while stacks are maintained by continuing to attack/cast.
Recast Q and E on cooldown for the rest of the 15s window (cooldowns 4-8s each at higher ranks), interspersed with autos to keep Darkness Rise active and maximize aura uptime.

Do not cast Indestructible (W) offensively in the damage fight — it produces no direct damage and its passive shield/heal conversion only matters for the survival fight; skip it entirely when optimizing damage output.
questions: Should R be used at all in a single 15s damage-fight simulation given its long cooldown, or is it excluded on the assumption that ultimates are evaluated separately/not assumed available?

Is the assumed ability rank/level for a 15s dummy fight max rank on Q/W/E (5) and R (3), or should it match the champion's overall level progression (e.g. only some ranks available depending on level)?

Should the simulator assume Mordekaiser starts the fight already at 3 Darkness Rise stacks (from a hypothetical pre-fight instance) or strictly at 0 stacks, since stack ramp-up meaningfully changes early damage in a short 15s window?

Given E's cast time (0.25s) plus a further 0.5s delay before the claw deals damage, and Q's 0.5s cast time, how should ability queueing/animation cancels be modeled to determine the actual number of casts obtainable in 15 seconds?
